claim: EGGI is a SEVEN-row frame table, not a single record. The label sits on the first row only and the six continuation rows are unlabelled, which is why a label-keyed reading stops at one: `EGGI FDB CEGGUP,$00FA,EGGUP` (:2255), then CEGGLF/$00FB/EGGLF (:2256), CEGGRT/$00FB/EGGRT (:2257), CEGGUP/$00FB/EGGB1 (:2258), CEGGMN/$FFF6/EGGB2 (:2259), CEGGMN/$FEF5/EGGB3 (:2260), CEGGMN/$00F5/PLY4S (:2261). The block's own header comment names the two halves: "EGG STILLS & HATCHING" (:2253). Rows 0-2 are the tumble stills, rows 3-5 the hatch stages, row 6 the dismounted standing rider. The table ends at :2261 — :2262 is a comment line, not an FDB.

An egg carries NO stored frame. WEGG recomputes the picture every frame from the egg's two velocities and stores only the resulting pointer: `LDA PVELX,U / BPL WEGRIT` selects the offset table by the SIGN of the X velocity, `LDD PVELY,U` then compares the Y velocity against $0080, and WEGPAR does `LDY EGGI / LEAY A,Y / STY PPICH,U` (:3527-3529) — the chosen byte offset indexes the EGGI table and only PPICH is written. This is why porting the frame choice needs no new field on the egg's state.

EGFLFT and EGFRIT are byte offsets into EGGI and are MIRRORED. `EGFLFT FCB 0,12,6  FALLING LEFT` (:3535) and `EGFRIT FCB 0,6,12  FALLING RIGHT` (:3536): both share slot 0 (offset 0, the level frame CEGGUP) and swap slots 1 and 2. An EGGI row is three FDB words = 6 bytes, so 0/6/12 index rows 0/1/2 — CEGGUP, CEGGLF, CEGGRT. Slot 2 is the fast-FALL frame and slot 1 the fast-RISE frame, so a falling egg tilts one way and a rising egg the other.

The level-frame boundary is ASYMMETRIC, and both edges are a BGT against zero. On the falling side `SUBD #$0080 / BGT WEGD2` (:3516-3517) means velY = 128 yields 0, BGT fails, and control falls into WEGUP — so 128 is still the LEVEL frame. On the rising side `ADDD #$0080 / BGT WEGUP` (:3524-3525) means velY = -128 also yields 0 and BGT also fails, but here the fall-through reaches WEGD3 (`LDA 1,Y`, :3526) — so -128 is already a fast RISE. The identical zero test lands on opposite sides because one path branches toward the level frame and the other away from it. A symmetric |velY| <= $0080 reading is therefore wrong at exactly -128.

EGGTBL is the egg's HATCH-animation driver — the THIRD table in the EGG ANIMATION TABLE block (:3533), after EGFLFT/EGFRIT, and the one that consumes EGGI rows 3-6. Eight rows, each `[col0, col1, col2]` (:3537-3544): `EGGTBL FCB 6,6,7  WIGGLE LEFT` / 0,6,3 WIGGLE UP / 12,6,7 WIGGLE RIGHT / 0,6,7+60 WIGGLE UP & PAUSE / 18,6,7 HATCH 1 / 24,11,7 HATCH 2 / 30,11,7 HATCH 3 / 36,11,0 HATCH 4. col0 is a byte offset into EGGI (row × 6), so 0/6/12/18/24/30/36 name rows 0/1/2/3/4/5/6 — EGGI, EGGLF, EGGRT, EGGB1, EGGB2, EGGB3, PLY4S. The maximum offset 36 → row 6 independently CORROBORATES EGGI's seven-row extent (JT87-001) from a different table. The walk runs straight through once; the block ends at :3544, the next header (BUZARD SEEKING MAN) is :3546.

EGGMAN walks EGGTBL a COLUMN at a time, and the three columns mean different things (unlike EGFLFT/EGFRIT, whose three columns are all EGGI offsets). Setup: `LDX #EGGTBL / STX PRDIR,U` (:3290-3291). Per row (:3297-3307): col0 is the FRAME offset — `LDA [PRDIR,U]  GET NEXT FRAME OFFSET` (:3299) then `JSR WEGPAR` draws it (:3300); col1 is the collision HEIGHT — `LDA PPOSY+1,U / STA PCOLY1,U / SUBA 1,X / STA PCOLY2,U` (:3302-3305); col2 is the DURATION and the terminator — `LDA 2,X / BNE EGGHCH` (:3306-3307), and `EGGHCH LEAX 3,X / … / JSR VNAPTPC` (:3294-3296) advances three bytes and naps col2. VNAPTPC is the same nap primitive PCNAP expands to (LDA #TIME / JSR VNAPTPC, RAMDEF.SRC:31-33), so col2 is a frame count. A col2 of 0 (HATCH 4) ends the walk.
